thread:
alex: Kicked off a stride-playback run against prod-traces v2 (anon, 0.5% sample). Goal: apples-to-apples compare kernel-selection + batching heuristics vs baseline kernels.
mike: Nice. Which flags did you use for deterministic replay? we should pin seeds and kv-warmup behavior.
jia: Command I used:
```
./harness --trace-dir s3://redwood/prod-scrubbed/v2 \
  --anon --sample 0.005 --seed 42 \
  --kv-warmup=true --kv-warmup-steps=16 \
  --kernel-policy=stride_auto --batch-hints=latency
```
sam: kv-warmup-steps=16 feels low for long contexts, did you look at prefix lengths distribution? :thinking_face:
alex: yes, median prefix ~48, 95th ~512 — warmup 16 was intentional to measure degradation when warmup under-provisioned.
trace-harness-bot: run 2654012345 started · workers=24 · target-qps=120 · mode=stride_playback
mike: Observed early divergence at step ~1200 — token-level latency p95 spikes +20% on stride_auto vs baseline.
jia: Did you capture perf counters? I want kernel occupancy and L2 miss rate. Also collect kv-cache hit ratio per request id.
alex: pushed a profiling snapshot: s3://redwood/profiles/2654012345/snapshot-1.json · contains nvprof dumps + internal timing.
qa-bot: parity-checks queued: deterministic checks, output-compare (token hashes), and checksum-against-baseline.
sam: Quick grep of logs shows kernel fallback to int8_fast on some layers (because dynamic quant path triggered). That changed execution path.
mike: That explains p95 — quantized kernel has higher tail due to reduced occupancy for batched short sequences.
jia: Suggestion: rerun with `--force-kernel=fp16_native` and `--batch-hints=throughput` to compare.
alex: Agree. Also we should run synthetic-traffic smoke to confirm if issue is replay-specific or general workload shape. I'll enqueue a synthetic run with same sequence length histogram.
trace-harness-bot: run 2654012365 (synthetic-smoke) started · workers=24 · target-qps=120
mike: For apples-to-apples, make sure model params and tokenizer versions match exactly. We had a minor tokenizer patch last week that changed spacing, which affects KV reuse.
alex: noted. pinned model sha and tokenizer sha in run metadata.
jia: For determinism, we need to verify KV cache warmup ordering: record first-request kv-populate events and compare checksums between runs.
sam: Also add a small random jitter to scheduling to rule out artificial alignment in replay harness.
alex: plan: (1) rerun with forced kernel (fp16_native) and throughput batching; (2) synthetic run with identical length histogram; (3) parity/determinism checks (token-hashes + kv-pop checks); (4) if regression persists, bisect kernel commits.
mike: timeline? can we get preliminary results in 2 hours? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
alex: will have synthetic + forced-kernel results in ~90m. posting artifacts and quick diff when done.
trace-harness-bot: run 2654012380 (forced-kernel) completed · exit=0 · p50=9ms p95=42ms p99=110ms
qa-bot: parity summary for 2654012345:
- deterministic: fail at 1203 (token hash mismatch)
- kv-check: mismatch in warmup entries for 0.7% of requests
- action: schedule deeper bisect
mike: thanks — looks like a warmup ordering + kernel-selection combo. I'll start a bisect on kernel selector config.
jia: I'll prepare a short notebook to aggregate per-request kv-hit-ratio vs latency and attach to the run artifacts.
alex: thanks team. keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
